content: On March 23, 2014, the Ministry of Health in Guinea informed the World Health Organization (WHO) about a rapidly escalating outbreak of Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) in the southeastern forested regions of Guinea, specifically in the districts of Guekedou, Macenta, Nzerekore, and Kissidougou. By March 22, 2014, there were 49 reported cases, including 29 fatalities, resulting in a case fatality rate of 59%. Among the deceased were four healthcare workers. Concurrently, suspected cases in border regions of Liberia and Sierra Leone were under investigation. Six blood samples from Guinea were analyzed at the Institut Pasteur in Lyon, France, and all tested positive for the Ebola virus via polymerase chain reaction (PCR). This confirmed the first outbreak of Ebola Virus Disease in Guinea. Genetic sequencing of the L gene revealed a strong similarity to the Zaire ebolavirus strain. Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) from Switzerland established isolation facilities in the affected areas and facilitated the transport of biological samples from suspected cases and their contacts to international reference laboratories for urgent testing. On March 30, 2014, the Ministry of Health in Liberia provided updated information on suspected and confirmed Ebola cases in the country. By March 29, seven clinical samples from adult patients in Foya district, Lofa County, were tested using PCR with primers specific to the Zaire ebolavirus strain at the mobile laboratory of the Institut Pasteur in Dakar, located in Conakry. Two of these samples tested positive for the Ebola virus. Among the suspected cases, there were two deaths: a 35-year-old woman who died on March 21 and tested positive for the virus, and a male patient who died on March 27 but tested negative. At that time, Foya was the only district in Liberia reporting confirmed or suspected cases of Ebola Hemorrhagic Fever. As of March 26, Liberia was monitoring 27 contacts under medical observation. A high-level National Task Force was established in Liberia to coordinate the response, with support from WHO, the International Red Cross (IRC), Samaritan’s Purse (SP) Liberia, Pentecostal Mission Unlimited (PMU)-Liberia, CHF-WASH Liberia, PLAN-Liberia, UNFPA, and UNICEF. On April 3, 2014, the outbreak was confirmed to be caused by a strain of the Ebola virus with a 98% genetic similarity to the Zaire ebolavirus. This marked the first time the disease had been detected in West Africa. By June 17, 2014, Guinea reported seven new cases and five new deaths, with cases distributed in Gueckedou (four cases and five deaths) and Boffa (three cases and no deaths). The cumulative total in Guinea reached 398 cases (254 confirmed, 88 probable, and 56 suspected) and 264 deaths. The geographical distribution of cases and deaths in Guinea was as follows: Conakry (70 cases and 33 deaths), Guéckédou (224 cases and 173 deaths), Macenta (41 cases and 28 deaths), Dabola (4 cases and 4 deaths), Kissidougou (8 cases and 5 deaths), Dinguiraye (1 case and 1 death), Telimele (30 cases and 9 deaths), Boffa (19 cases and 10 deaths), and Kouroussa (1 case and 1 death). At that time, 24 patients were receiving treatment in EVD centers located in Conakry (6), Guéckédou (9), Telimele (3), and Boffa (6). A total of 1,258 contacts were under medical follow-up across the country, distributed as follows: Conakry (252), Guéckédou (529), Macenta (52), Telimele (118), Dubreka (118), and Boffa (189). Since the beginning of the outbreak, 69.4% of registered contacts (2,848 out of 4,106) had completed the mandatory 21-day observation period. In Liberia, nine new cases and five new deaths were reported, with cases distributed in Lofa (six cases and no deaths) and Montserrado (three cases and five deaths). This brought the cumulative total in Liberia to 33 cases (18 confirmed, 8 probable, and 7 suspected) and 24 deaths. The geographical distribution of cases and deaths in Liberia was as follows: Lofa (21 cases and 14 deaths), Montserrado (8 cases and 8 deaths), Margibi (2 cases and 2 deaths), and Nimba (2 cases and no deaths). Five patients were receiving treatment in EVD centers in Lofa. A total of 108 contacts were under medical follow-up, distributed as follows: Lofa (95) and Montserrado (13). Since the beginning of the outbreak, 41.5% of registered contacts (108 out of 260) had completed the mandatory 21-day observation period. In Sierra Leone, 31 new cases and four new deaths were reported, with cases distributed in Kailahun (29 cases and 4 deaths), Kono (1 case), and Western (1 case). This brought the cumulative total in Sierra Leone to 97 cases (92 confirmed, 3 probable, and 2 suspected) and 49 deaths. The geographical distribution of cases and deaths in Sierra Leone was as follows: Kailahun (92 cases and 46 deaths), Kambia (1 case and no deaths), Port Loko (2 cases and 1 death), Kono (1 case and no deaths), and Western (1 case and 1 death). Thirty-three patients were receiving treatment in the EVD center in Kenema. A total of 37 contacts were under medical follow-up in Kailahun, and contact tracing efforts were ongoing in Kailahun, Kambia, and Port Loko.
